newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 31.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:

* Several mysteries, including the death of a Filipino prospector, surround the story of Canada's Bre-X Minerals, which recently announced that a mine in Indonesia contained less gold than orignally thought.
* The National Science Foundation intends to reduce the number of supercomputer research centers it finances from four to two.
* Analysts see new hurdles for the 1990s bull market and the possibility of a significant downturn.
* The amount of electronic mail has made electronic discovery in lawsuits an industry in itself, lawyers say.
* Studies show U.S. farm workers' wages have trailed inflation for the past 20 years.
* Three novels set in Silicon Valley talk about the emerging culture there.
* The Roman Catholic Church has entered the debate on the impact of advertising on society.
* Broadcasting: News Corp's Fox might surpass Walt Disney's ABC this year in terms of ad revenue per program and could make ground on General Electric's NBC.
* United Press International is trying to strengthen its radio broadcast operations and aims to sell fragments of news to customers.
* Two biologists have received a patent that seems to be for recovering not just ancient bacteria but other organisms found in amber or other resins.
* Three-dimensional computer aided design and manufacturing programs are turning up in unlikely places.
